Did you know that beyond its endless ocean views and sun-kissed vibes, California also has a dark, spooky side? Across the state, mysterious legends and paranormal spots offer unforgettable haunted experiences for the brave-hearted. Whether or not you believe in ghosts, visiting these 7 spooky spots across the Golden State, listed from north to south, is sure to deliver a chilling thrill.

Haunted Places For Every Adventure lover to visit in California

Every place is a dream in the USA if you are visiting for the first time. For those who are looking to add fun and adventure with horror stories to the vacation, these are the top destinations known for their scary moves and looks you need to check out.

1. Preston Castle, Ione

The castle’s foreboding facade looks straight out of a horror film. Once a reform school for unruly youth and abandoned children, the structure’s sinister history includes corporal punishment, toxic dunking baths, and a housekeeper’s murder. Open for tours year-round, the Amador County castle turns into a full-fledged haunted house in September.

2. Bodie State Historic Park, Bodie

Spanning 500 acres in Mono County, about 75 miles southeast of Lake Tahoe, Bodie is a Gol Rush–era ghost town frozen in time. More than 100 structures remain, as do the supposed spirits of prospectors. While dishware shards and nails can be found on the streets, anyone who takes home a souvenir risks the curse of Bodie, and it is also against park rules.

3. Winchester Mystery House, San Jose

A door that leads to nowhere and a staircase that dead-ends into the ceiling? It is said that widow Sarah Winchester designed the house this peculiar way to confuse the ghosts: men killed by her late husband’s creation, the Winchester rifle.

4. Point Sur Lighthouse, Big Sur

This picturesque lighthouse has been illuminating the waters off the coast of Big Sur since 1889. Perhaps it is the original keeper who some believe still visits the site in his original uniform. Moonlight tours are available for the brave and the curious.

5. Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel, Los Angeles

Stay at the swanky Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel for a chance to glimpse one of the most glamorous ghosts of all time. It is said that Marilyn Monroe herself still haunts the halls. Guests have also reported mysterious trumpet music believed to be the spirit of Montgomery Clift, who liked to practice in suite 928.

6. The Queen Mary, Long Beach

Once known as the “Grey Ghost,” the Queen Mary serves up chills in the form of screams from a decapitated sailor in the boiler room and visions of a lady in white roaming the halls. Visitors can choose from a handful of haunted tours, or book a stay in Stateroom B340 for overnight thrills.

7. Hotel del Coronado, San Diego

In 1892, 24-year-old Kate Morgan checked into this luxurious waterfront resort alone and then ended her life on the hotel’s staircase. Many guests have experienced strange breezes, flickering lights, and phantom footsteps believed to be evidence of the young woman’s unrest.

Editor's Pick

Whether you are chasing genuine paranormal encounters or simply love exploring places rich with eerie history, California’s haunted landmarks offer a thrilling detour from the usual tourist trail. From windswept coastal lighthouses and Gold Rush ghost towns to iconic Hollywood hotels, each stop adds a spine-tingling layer of mystery to your Golden State itinerary proving that sometimes the most unforgettable travel memories happen after dark.

FAQ

1. Which is the most haunted place to visit in California?The Queen Mary in Long Beach and the Winchester Mystery House in San Jose are widely considered California's most active paranormal hotspots.

2. Can you stay overnight at haunted hotels in California?Yes, iconic properties like the Hollywood Roosevelt Hotel, The Queen Mary, and Hotel del Coronado offer overnight stays alongside ghost tours.

3. What is the best time of year to visit California's haunted spots?September and October are the most popular months for special after-dark ghost tours, though most historic sites remain open year-round.
